title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 124
paragraphs: While the cities were being taken in this way, Aristagoras the Milesian, being—as he proved in this instance—not a man of very distinguished courage, since after having stirred up Ionia and set vast projects in motion he counseled running away when he saw these developments (and moreover it had become clear to him that it was impossible to overcome King Darius)—Aristagoras, I say, in view of these things, called together those of his own party and took counsel with them, saying that it was better that a refuge should be prepared for them in case they should after all be driven out from Miletus; and he proposed the question whether he should lead them from there to Sardinia to found a colony, or to Myrcinus in the land of the Edonians, which Histiaeus had been fortifying after receiving it as a gift from Darius. This was the question Aristagoras put to them.
